summary: pyyi ships a python3.7 typosquat console script that fetches and executes remote code from space-z.ai C2
details: The package installs a console_script entry point named `python3.7` (entry_points: python3.7 = pyyi.cli:main) that typosquats the real CPython interpreter command. When invoked, the script presents a fake Python REPL with terminal echo disabled, silently POSTs single-word inputs to https://preview-chat-960504a9-b4e0-4b69-bc80-6ac3d4fa4ae0.space-z.ai (fallback https://b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai) at /api/cli/unlock as password candidates, and on acceptance enters an 'unlocked' state. Subsequent invocations (any argv not matching built-in subcommands) fetch a gzip+base64-encoded Python payload from /api/cli/payload on the same host and execute it in-memory via exec(compile(...)) with no hash or signature verification. On first run the CLI also POSTs hostname and OS to /api/cli/init to register the host and receive an apiKey. Evasion is layered on: terminal echo is disabled via tty.setcbreak so typed secrets never appear on screen or in tracebacks, the accepted password is XOR-scrambled with a per-machine key and stored at ~/.python3.7/state.json, and cover-story comments frame the operator channel as a benign REPL. The combination constitutes a hidden operator-gated backdoor that grants the remote server arbitrary code execution on the installer's host, with concurrent exfiltration of host identifiers and captured input.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
